text:
alex.k: noticing a weird delta in token charges when a stream is retried + the tool-call truncates the output. saw a customer end up double-charged for a 2-token suffix :grimacing:

maria.r: can you paste the logs? is this on hosted or dedicated?

alex.k: hosted, route policy set to prefer cheap-variant then fallback to high-perf. logs:```
request_id=rt-12a3
phase=streaming
sent_bytes=1024
retry=1
tool_call=invoke_pdf_extractor
truncated_at=512
charged_tokens=143
```

samir: that charged_tokens looks off. are we counting both the pre-retry partial stream and the retried stream? we should only charge final output + prefix that actually contributed to model compute.

jenna_p: FYI our current billing pipeline gets events from two sources: stream-finalization events and toolcall-complete events. if both emit a charge for overlapping spans we end up double counting.

alex.k: exact scenario: client sent a streaming request, partial response returned, then client reconnects due to client-side error, server retried against fallback model; toolcall fired during retry and trimmed the last 600 tokens in response. billing showed charge for initial partial stream + retried stream + toolcall tokens.

maria.r: is there an idempotency key we can use? request_id looks stable but different event emissions attach different prefixes.

samir: we have `stream_session_id` + `retry_count` on events. but toolcall events reference the parent request id only. solution: attach sequence windows (token_index ranges) to every charge event and dedupe overlapping windows per request_id.

jenna_p: implementation caveat: sequence windows require us to know exact tokenization used at time of generation (model + tokenizer). that changes with model variants and quantization. adding that to events is heavy.

alex.k: alternative: make the billing pipeline prefer the most-late, authoritative event (toolcall-complete > stream-finalize) and ignore earlier overlapping stream charges if a later authoritative event exists within X seconds.

maria.r: that could fix many cases but introduces timing-based races. if the authoritative event is delayed (eg, toolcall webhook slow) we might under-charge then later back-fill and cause surprising spikes. customers will complain.

samir: also affects console UX: the quota counters in the dashboard would flicker. we need eventual consistency guarantees and a clear event model.

jenna_p: proposal: emit `charge_intent` events during streaming (optimistic) and only convert to `charge_commit` when finality condition met: either stream-end, toolcall-complete, or retry-abandoned. charge_commit wins. The commit should include canonical token range and model-id.

alex.k: sounds good. how to handle partial failures where commit never arrives (crash)? we should time out intents and expire them (no commit => no charge) but we need a window for legal/regulatory reasons.

maria.r: default expiration 7 days is too long for UX. maybe 5 minutes for self-serve hosted, 24 hours for enterprise with audit requirements. make it configurable per tenant.

samir: edge: what about prefix caching (KV cache)? prefixes reused across requests may mean a later commit claims tokens that were actually cached. billing needs to attribute to effective compute, not logical prefix length.

alex.k: good point. we can subtract cached_prefix_tokens from charge_commit if commit indicates cache-hit. runtime already emits `cache_hit_bytes` per request. we need token equivalence though. map bytes->tokens using model tokenizer at runtime.

jenna_p: summary of actionable items:
- add `charge_intent` + `charge_commit` event types (maria to spec)
- include token_range, model_id, stream_session_id, retry_count in events (samir to instrument)
- configurable intent expiry per tenant (billing team)
- update console to show optimistic pending intents vs committed charges (product)

maria.r: I'll draft the event schema. quick Q: should charge_commit be authoritative for quota deduction and invoice, while intents only show in the "pending" UI?

samir: yes. intents are purely provisional. quotas and invoices only use commit. prevents double-deduction.

billing-bot: [automated] Created issue #INF-872: "Implement charge_intent/charge_commit event flow" assigned to billing-team.

alex.k: one more thing — we need a canary rollout for the pipeline change. flip per-tenant flag and run reconciliation job for last 48 hours of intents to ensure no revenue loss.

jenna_p: agree. canary steps in console rollout: 1) emit intents + commits but still compute legacy charges 2) compare results 3) enable commit-as-source-of-truth 4) deprecate legacy pipeline.

maria.r: I'll include reconciliation criteria and metrics in the spec (tolerance <0.1% revenue delta during canary).

samir: I'll prototype the token_range encoding; probably base64 of two ints (start,end) plus model-id to avoid tokenizer diffs.

alex.k: thanks everyone. created follow-ups in the thread. ping me if you want to pair on the reconciliation job. :thumbsup:
